MANILA, Philippines – World No. 1 pickleball player Anna Leigh Waters makes a quick return to the Philippines.

Following a well-received debut tour in Manila last October, Waters will next grace the legendary Araneta Coliseum on December 9 with a series of world-class exhibitions and other activities, while organizers have also promised musical performances with celebrity guests.

“The moment Anna Leigh Waters stepped onto Philippine soil last October, the clamor from fans and players was electric,” organizers shared in an official statement on Thursday, November 5. “We quickly realized that an ordinary venue simply wouldn’t suffice.

“Moving this showcase to the Smart Araneta Coliseum was an easy decision driven entirely by the overwhelming public demand. We want to ensure that as many fans as possible have the opportunity to witness the world’s greatest pickleball player in action, live.”

blocks.caption: How world No. 1 Anna Leigh Waters balances life and pickleball

blocks.text: General ticket sales for the event presented by wellness brand IAM Worldwide begin on Monday, November 9, following a limited exclusive sale period this Thursday, November 5.

“Pickleball is more than just a game to me. It’s speed, focus, and endurance, all in one. That’s why I am more than willing to support a community that values performance and wellness together,” the 19-year-old American sensation said in a video release.

“Let’s celebrate sports, health, and the power of staying strong together,” added the teenage prodigy, who has been the all-time women’s pickleball pro title record holder since October 2022 at age 15.

Waters has also been the undisputed pickleball pro title record holder since November 2025, after eclipsing doubles partner and men’s world No. 1 Ben Johns, and has since won an unprecedented 200th career title at the 2026 PPA Veolia Chicago Cup last October.

Passionate Filipino fans arrived in droves to meet the global face of pickleball in her last foray on Manila soil, as Waters joined packed crowds in various Taguig and Makati sports apparel stores last October 13 to 15.

Already part of TIME100’s Most Influential People in Sports, the young Waters also gamely shared her life success story to fans and media, and encouraged Filipino players to fully enjoy and embrace the process of the rising sport. – Rappler.com

articles.title: The Pitt and ER are similar enough for lawsuit to proceed, judge rules
articles.summary: The widow of ER creator Michael Crichton argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the 1990s series.

blocks.text: US drama The Pitt is similar enough to medical series ER for a lawsuit against its producers to progress, a court in the US has ruled.
The widow of Michael Crichton, who created ER, argues The Pitt is effectively a reboot of the series, which has been made without proper permission or credit.
Sherri Crichton says her husband's contract included a "frozen rights" provision that prohibited any spin-offs, sequels or reboots of ER being made without his express consent.

A three-judge panel said there are "clear and numerous similarities between The Pitt and ER," which means the case can go ahead. Warner Bros previously described the lawsuit as "baseless" and sought to have it dismissed.

Listing the similarities between the two shows, the court cited the emergency room setting, the fast pace, use of medical jargon, graphic depictions of injuries, and younger doctors fresh from medical school being trained.
"We find the details here suffice for a prima facie case," the judges said.
It means the case will now go to a jury trial in Los Angeles Superior Court.
But the judges dismissed separate claims against actor-producer Noah Wyle, executive producer John Wells and showrunner R Scott Gemmill.
The justices said there was insufficient evidence to show the three producers were aware they could be violating Crichton's contractual rights.
ER launched in 1994, based on original screenplay written by Crichton. It starred George Clooney, Anthony Edwards, Eriq La Salle and Maria Bello, and aired 331 episodes over the next 15 years.
The show, which followed a group of doctors working in an emergency room in Chicago, was a hit with viewers and critics, and won 23 Emmy Awards during its run including outstanding drama series.
Discussions about a possible reboot of the show began in 2020, and studio Warner Bros spent months negotiating with Crichton's estate.
Those talks were reported to have collapsed over credit and financial guarantees, and producers began developing The Pitt in its place.

But Sherri Crichton and the John Michael Crichton Trust argue the show is a rebranded but uncredited reboot of ER, using the same formula, pacing, style and setting, rather than an entirely original series.
They said producers "simply moved the show from Chicago to Pittsburgh, rebranded it The Pitt, and ploughed ahead without any attribution or compensation for Crichton and his heirs".
Many actors and creatives from ER also work on The Pitt, including Wyle, Gemmill and Wells.

After legal action began in 2024, Warner Bros Television said in a statement that the lawsuit was "baseless", arguing that The Pitt was a "new and original show", adding that the studio would "vigorously defend against these meritless claims".
But in a 33-page opinion published on Wednesday, a three-judge panel unanimously upheld an earlier ruling that Crichton's estate had presented enough evidence to pursue its claim.
Warner Bros had sought to have the lawsuit dismissed on appeal, arguing the shows shared only "generic similarities" common to "any dramatic story involving emergency room doctors".

The judges said they had compared the opening episode scripts for the two shows and found sufficient similarities in plot, themes, dialogue, mood, setting, pace, characters, graphic injury detail and sequence of events.

Sherri Crichton said: "I am deeply gratified by the Court of Appeal decision and look forward to discovery and to our case, which affects writers, creators, and their families and estates, being presented to a jury."
Warner Bros has not yet commented on the latest ruling.

articles.title: North Korea tells EU to 'mind its own business' on human rights
articles.summary: North Korea's UN mission has lashed out at the European Union over a draft UN resolution. Pyongyang has said the West does not have a monopoly on human rights.

image.caption: Under Kim Jong Un's regime, North Korea is one of the most restrictive countries in the worldImage: KCNA/KNS/AFP

blocks.text: North Korea, responded European Union's draft United Nations resolution on human rights in the country by telling the bloc to "mind its own business," state media reported Thursday.
Pyongyang has long been accused by the UN and human rights advocates of committing human rights violations.
North Korea's UN mission said in a statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency that the move was a "farce" and a "politically motivated provocation."
It said the resolution is "flagrantly distorting it's human rights policy," claiming that human rights are not "a monopoly of the West."
Referring to the protests in Europe, "Streets are filled with demonstrators from all walks of life demanding such elementary rights as the rights to existence," the North Korean mission said.
"The EU had better mind its own business, instead of hyping up the non-existent 'human rights issues,'" it added.
South Korea to co-sponsor the resolution
The UN General Assembly has adopted a resolution condemning North Korea's human rights violations every year since 2005.
According to the South Korean Yonhap News Agency, Seoul has decided to co-sponsor the resolution proposed by the EU.
It is the fifth consecutive year that Seoul has done so, following a break from 2019 to 2021 under the liberal Moon Jae-in government.
The draft text is expected to be adopted by the Third Committee of the UN General Assembly later this month, before being submitted to the UN General Assembly for final approval.

articles.title: How communities in Cebu marked Tino’s first anniversary
articles.summary: Through the Padayon Cebu chatroom on Muni, Cebuanos revisit the devastation of Typhoon Tino, share updates on affected communities, and call for lasting solutions a year after

items: A year after Typhoon Tino, residents in Cebu continue to face flooding, unsafe living conditions, and trauma from the disaster, with many still lacking safe, permanent relocation.
Discussions among survivors highlighted ongoing concerns about flood-control accountability and the need for urgent flood-management measures, which remain largely unimplemented.

Community dialogues and activities around the anniversary emphasized the importance of transparency in flood-control spending and the necessity for comprehensive disaster rehabilitation that goes beyond just housing.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – A year after Typhoon Tino devastated communities across Cebu, residents are still grappling with flooding, unsafe living conditions, and questions over flood-control efforts.

These concerns took center stage in the Padayon Cebu chat room on Muni in the Rappler app, where survivors shared stories, discussed conditions in affected communities, and highlighted activities that marked the first anniversary of Typhoon Tino on Wednesday, November 4.

Leading up to the anniversary, Cebuanos in the chat room initiated a discussion titled “Isang taon matapos ang Tino, kamusta na ang Cebu?” (How is Cebu a year after Typhoon Tino?). They reflected on the devastation of the disaster, and discussed the challenges that affected communities continue to face a year later.

Cebu-based Mover Jerome Valdez shared the story of Alma Quingco, 46, from Barangay Maslog, Danao City, who was on duty at the University of the Philippines Cebu when Tino struck. When she returned home, floodwaters had made their house inaccessible, and many of their belongings had been swept away.

“Despite the help, the experience left a lasting impact. Alma shared that there are still fears and trauma associated with what happened. Even now, the memory of how quickly the floodwaters rose remains with her,” Valdez shared in the chat room.

The discussion also brought attention to villages in Tambisan, where severe flooding continues even during ordinary rainfall, and families who remain without safe, permanent relocation a year after their homes were destroyed.

Violy Musngi of La Paloma Village, during Rappler’s #MoveCebu roadshow in October, recalled how residents were caught off guard by Typhoon Tino, with floodwaters reaching waist-deep levels in her area and rising above head level in Tambisan.

“We were surprised by the waist-deep flooding, which persisted even after Typhoon Tino. Residents in Tambisan are also suffering from leptospirosis. After Tino, there’s flooding after flooding. Even light rains now cause flooding almost immediately,” Musngi said during the forum.
Reymarr Hijara of the Movement for a Livable Cebu (MLC) also joined the online discussion. MLC is a civic group in Cebu, advocating for safer and more sustainable flood management.

In November 2025, they proposed a petition for urgent flood-management measures, including the creation of a Cebu Floodwater Management Office, relocation of families from high-risk areas, protection of watersheds, and a review of flood-control structures. The group also called for no-build zones in areas inundated during Tino.
But even a year later, according to Hijara, implementing the six proposed flood-management actions remained largely unfinished or unverified a year after Tino.

The most concrete development, he said, was MLC’s invitation to join the Provincial Flood Control and Drainage Task Force, created under Executive Order 74 after the November 2025 flooding. However, Hijara stressed that the task force’s formation and MLC’s participation did not amount to implementation of the group’s proposed measures.
“A task force is not yet implementation,” Hijara said in the chat room.

The discussions in Padayon Cebu also highlighted two activities around the November 4 anniversary: a multi-stakeholder dialogue on flood-control accountability and a sustainability walk through downtown Cebu.

To examine urban vulnerabilities, University of the Philippines (UP) Cebu’s College of Communication, Art, and Design (CCAD), together with participants from the University of the Philippines Open University and Japan’s Meiji University, held a walk through downtown Cebu.

The guided walk passed through areas including San Nicolas, Pasil, Taboan, Carbon Market, Plaza Independencia, and Colon, examining Cebu’s built environment, public spaces, transportation systems, and cultural heritage.

According to an announcement by UP Cebu’s CCAD, Tino’s severe flooding served as a point of reflection as participants considered how cities can adapt to flooding and extreme heat while preserving their cultural identity.
The walk also drew comparisons between climate adaptation approaches in the Philippines and Japan, including lessons Cebu could apply to building safer and more livable communities.
Aside from a community walk, various groups also organized a dialogue to discuss the pressing concerns among survivors.

The dialogue titled, “Kahinumdom pa mo namo? (Do you still remember us?) A Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue on Flood Control Accountability and the Continuing Concerns on Typhoon Tino Survivors,” was organized by Sugbuanong Pakigbisog Kontra Kurapsyon (SuPaKK) in collaboration with partner organizations.

During the dialogue, John Roy Rigodon of the Sectoral Transparency Alliance on Natural Resource Governance (STANCe) shared findings from visits to communities along major rivers in Cebu, including the Kinalawan River in Toledo City and the Cotcot River in Liloan and Compostela, where he examined the situation of residents living in flood-prone areas a year after Tino.
According to Rigodon, the communities continue to face concerns over their safety when typhoons hit. This includes being at risk to flooding and lack of safe and permanent relocation.
“Will they be safe in the next typhoon?” he asked, pointing to relocation as a major concern among residents.

The dialogue also raised questions about flood-control spending. Organizers cited P17.4 billion in major river flood-control projects from 2016 to 2025, including P11.1 billion for the Butuanon River, and called for transparency and accountability. These figures were also reported in a SunStar Cebu investigation on how Tino’s floods exposed how flood control projects failed in Cebu.

Moreover, Norika Ishikawa of the Cebu Anti-Corruption Coalition and Center for Emergency Aid, Rehabilitation and Development Inc.(CONCERN) questioned how the government would lead rehabilitation efforts for Tino-affected communities amid reported cuts to disaster rehabilitation and housing funds for 2027.
She said recovery must go beyond providing houses, calling for safe and affordable housing with access to livelihoods, utilities, roads, hospitals, and schools.
“Disaster rehabilitation is not an expense. Building back better is a public investment,” Ishikawa said.

Ishikawa said the next steps identified during the dialogue include formulating a relocation agenda with Tino-affected informal settler families and mobilizing for an accountability action on November 30.
“Nakakalungkot ang sharing, nakakagalit ang inaction, but hopeful pa rin (The sharing is saddening, the inaction is infuriating, but there is still hope),” she said.

Typhoon Tino caused widespread devastation in Cebu, affecting nearly 2 million people, displacing over 636,000, and resulting in 96 confirmed deaths with many still missing. It also damaged approximately 262,000 homes (over 24,000 totally destroyed), leaving affected communities struggling to recover a year later.
A year after Tino, affected communities still continue to call for safe relocation, transparent flood-control spending, and rehabilitation that addresses their long-term needs. – Rappler.com

articles.title: How elderly ‘unsung heroes’ powered Lula’s historic fightback in Brazil
articles.summary:
Older voters praised for helping tip balance in leftwing president’s favour against far-right Flávio Bolsonaro in runoff

It had been nearly a decade since Celia de Oliveira Soares last…
articles.byline: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro

blocks.text: It had been nearly a decade since Celia de Oliveira Soares last voted, and months since the 101-year-old great-grandmother last left her home.

But on 25 October, when Brazil held what many considered its most important presidential election in decades, relatives helped Soares into a wheelchair and drove her to a nearby school to make sure the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, did not prevail.
Soares clung to the banister as, step by step, she climbed two flights of stairs to the polling booth under the watchful eye of her granddaughter’s husband, Marcio Marques.
Inside, the frail but jaunty centenarian keyed the number “13” – representing Bolsonaro’s leftwing rival, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva – into an electronic voting machine and pressed confirm.
“I like Lula. I really do!” enthused Soares, a retired bank employee who has lived in Rio de Janeiro most of her life.

blocks.caption: Soares, with her granddaughter Poliana Soares Jordão, said she didn’t like the Bolsonaros, ‘so the efficient thing to to do was to go out and vote’. Photograph: João Laet/The Guardian

blocks.text: “I don’t like Bolsonaro or his father. So the efficient thing to do was go out and vote,” Soares added, as her grandsons, Tito and Ravi, played on the balcony around her surrounded by pot plants and books.
Soares is one of more than 1 million elderly people who, having missed the election’s 4 October first round – which Lula lost – decided to vote in the second.

Never since the return of democracy in the 1980s had the first-round loser bounced back, but Lula did just that. And after Lula’s shock revival, elderly voters have been hailed as the election’s unsung heroes – including by Lula himself.

At his 81st birthday party last week, the leftist veteran shed tears while describing his gratitude to the elderly people who helped him clinch a historic fourth term while clutching walking frames and sticks.

“I honestly think it was the most powerful and human image I’ve ever seen during an election,” Lula said of viral pictures showing voters in their 80s, 90s and 100s being carried into polling centres by relatives or carers, some in stretchers or wheelchairs.

In north-east Brazil, where Lula was born into rural poverty in the 1940s, a 114-year-old retiree called Josefa Pereira da Conceição went to vote wearing a red T-shirt emblazoned with Lula’s face and the slogan “Strength of the people”.
Election experts are still crunching the numbers to fully understand how Lula pulled off his unprecedented fightback, finding 10.3m extra votes between the first and second rounds.

Explanations include a sharp increase in welfare benefits on the eve of the vote; an extraordinary digital mobilisation involving a pro-Lula WhatsApp group that grew from 50,000 to nearly 11m members in less than a month; and a student-led street rebellion in which millions of citizens protested across Brazil.

Some believe elderly people were also crucial, noting how 1.4 million of the 3 million extra voters who took part in the second round after skipping the first were over 70. Pre-election polls suggested such voters were more inclined to vote for Lula.

blocks.caption: Lula wipes away tears as he thanks supporters during an event to celebrate his 81st birthday on 27 October.  Photograph: Eraldo Peres/AP

blocks.text: Speaking at Lula’s victory celebration, the former minister Simone Tebet called the result a cross-generational triumph which sent a message to the democratic world. “It is possible to resist fascism – all you need to do is mobilise society,” Tebet declared, claiming: “Young people hit the streets and golden-agers saved our democracy.”

The political journalist José Roberto de Toledo said there was concrete evidence of higher turnout among older voters in the runoff, particularly those aged 60 to 79. Voting is only mandatory in Brazil for those aged 18 to 69.

“The images [of elderly people voting] aren’t misleading: they reveal a phenomenon that isn’t just an isolated case. It’s not some made-up story or a staged example. It really happened – and it was a movement you can measure statistically,” Toledo said of the images suggesting an unusually large number of older voters.

That said, Toledo believed the swing to Lula was explained mostly by fear, not age. Voting data suggested many people who backed Lula in the runoff had previously voted for Bolsonaro’s rightwing adversaries, hoping to protest against Lula’s Worker’s party (PT), which has governed for nearly 18 of the last 24 years.

blocks.caption: Lea Zorzella, 90, left her hospital in São Paulo to vote in the runoff election. Photograph: Alexandre Meneghini/Reuters

blocks.text: In the runoff, faced with a straight choice between Lula, a familiar and predictable figure even for detractors, and Bolsonaro, who represented a leap into the unknown, many preferred the former.

“A protest vote in the first round [became] a safety vote or a lower-risk vote in the second – even if it wasn’t a happy vote,” said Toledo, who believed Bolsonaro alienated many voters with his “arrogant” behaviour after winning the first round.

Particularly damaging was the rightwinger’s authoritarian-sounding vow to “re-democratise” the already democratic country – something Toledo suspected stoked fears that Bolsonaro aspired to be “the emperor of Brazil”.

blocks.caption: An elderly voter at a polling station in Porto Alegre on 25 October. Photograph: Diego Vara/Reuters

blocks.text: Even before those remarks, Soares fretted over the direction Brazil might take under Flávio Bolsonaro, whose father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting to seize power after losing the 2022 election to Lula.

“His father wanted to stage a coup … and stay on as president, just like Getúlio [Vargas did in 1937],” recalled the great-grandmother, who was 12 at the time and lived through the subsequent eight years of dictatorial rule.
Marques, a 51-year-old food entrepreneur, said his grandmother-in-law was also critical of how Jair Bolsonaro undermined vaccination efforts during the Covid pandemic, when 700,000 Brazilians died.

“She’s got three great-grandchildren … and she understands she’s nearing the end of her life. But she’s worried about the country, about her family and about future generations,” said Marques, becoming visibly emotional as he recalled watching Soares exercise her democratic right, perhaps for the last time.

“It was so moving to see her strength and desire [to vote] … We felt she had an intuition, or something telling her she needed to be part of this … She doesn’t know if she’ll get another chance,” added Marques, whose 85-year-old father, Helço Muniz, also voted Lula – in his case for the first time.

Sitting in her armchair overlooking Rio’s Guanabara Bay, five days after the election, Soares voiced excitement that Lula would soon start his fourth and final term. “I’ve been fond of him ever since he was poor,” she said of the lathe operator turned president, who first took office as president in 2003. “He was poor and he became rich, but he carried on being a simple man.”
Occasionally, Soares’s memory betrayed her and she needed reminding that Lula had pulled off one of modern history’s greatest democratic comebacks. “But that’s wonderful!” she beamed.
Reminded of Lula’s feat, Soares predicted Bolsonaro would flee abroad.
“He’s already gone!” her granddaughter, Poliana Soares Jordão, 46, told her. “His dad’s in prison and he’s fled.”

Soares, who has lived through four coups, 16 presidential elections and four Lula wins, was not surprised. “He must have gone to the US, then,” the centenarian guessed, correctly. “He’d been getting ready for that for a while, hadn’t he?”

articles.title: Family of injured Wainwright soldier holds bedside vigil in burn unit
articles.summary: Pte. Liam Ramage, 27, of Red Deer, Alta., was one of dozens of service members hurt in an out-of-control grass fire at CFB Wainwright on Oct. 17.

blocks.text: Family of soldier severely burned at CFB Wainwright describes his ordeal
The mother of a soldier fighting to recover from severe burns he sustained in last month's CFB Wainwright fire says she worries not only about his physical injuries, but also his mental health.
Pte. Liam Ramage, 27, of Red Deer, Alta., was one of dozens of service members hurt in an out-of-control grass fire on the central Alberta military base on Oct. 17. Four died.
Roughly 40 per cent of Liam’s body was affected, mostly third- and fourth-degree burns, mainly to his face, neck and throat, according to his mother Cheryl Ramage.
“Some to his arms, really bad to his hands, the upper and the palms," she told CBC News in an interview this week. "Some of his legs, … some to his back and some to the top of his feet.
"They’re doing skin grafts to the majority. His eyelids even have skin grafts on them, so he can’t open his eyes.”
Cheryl Ramage, a nurse, said Liam's family is taking it day by day, knowing his recovery could take years. (Peter Evans/CBC)
Cheryl and Liam’s wife Marisa have been constants at his bedside at the University of Alberta Hospital in Edmonton. He can barely move, speak or see.
“Being locked in your own mind is a form of torture right?” said Cheryl, who’s a nurse. “His mental health is going to have to be addressed right away.”

items: Alberta government hosts remembrance ceremony as country mourns CFB Wainwright victims
Sask. soldier killed in CFB Wainwright fire remembered as funny, passionate at military funeral
In wake of Wainwright tragedy, this year's Silver Cross Mother has a message for grieving families

blocks.text: She describes the days since the fire as devastating.
Being a nurse can sometimes help her compartmentalize her feelings, but it doesn’t shield her from them, Cheryl said.

“I can kind of turn clinical. When I go into his room, especially if I’m with somebody else, I can be like, ‘This is what this line’s doing and that’s what this dressing is for.’ I can kind of remove myself from it, if that makes sense — I can just talk about the injuries, not looking at it like it’s my son. But if I’m there by myself or go home by myself, I’m a disaster."
‘Identified him by his toes’

Marisa said she first learned something might be wrong in a text from her father alerting her to the situation in Wainwright on the day of the fire. The last time she had heard from Liam was a text earlier in the day.

Cheryl’s other son Rowan, who was also training at CFB Wainwright, texted his mother to let her know he was OK. But she did not hear back from Liam. She went to Liam and Marisa’s house in Edmonton to wait for word.
Hours later, at around 3 a.m. local time the next day, warrant officers knocked on the door and gave them the terrible news — “a mother’s worst nightmare,” Cheryl said.
A photo of Marisa (left) and Liam (right) on March 31, 2024. Liam joined the military in March 2024 and went to basic training the following month. (Supplied by Marisa Ramage)
“I don’t think I stopped shaking for the entire amount of time that they were there,” Marisa said.
The pair rushed to the hospital.
“We couldn’t recognize his face,” Cheryl said. “He was completely covered in dressings and so swollen. He was not recognizable. We identified him by his toes.”
‘It’s so unpredictable’

Liam is fighting pneumonia. He has had three surgeries and three strokes, which paralyzed the left side of his body, though he’s showing some toe, hip and leg movement. He has necrosis — the death of body tissue — on several fingers, his ears and nose.
He can now breathe on his own, though he is placed on a ventilator at night to give his lungs a break. Thanks to a special device, he has been able to speak a few words in recent days.
“He mouthed my name when I was in there with my dad and that was shocking for me,” Marisa said. “I did have a really good cry after.”
Marisa and Liam started dating in 2020 and married in 2023. (Supplied by Marisa Ramage)
Both women say it’s hard to imagine what life will look like for Liam, an outgoing, active man who loves music, cooking and playing hockey.
“It is so unpredictable,” Cheryl said. “He’s got a stroke — is he going to be able to walk again? He’s got skin grafts — does he have to learn how to walk again? Is he going to lose his fingers?
“We really try to take it day to day. … We do know it’s going to be months and months and months — if not years — of recovery. But what that recovery looks like? We just can’t tell at this point.”
She worries about Liam's mental health; the deadly fire still haunts him.
“He does say he remembers it," Cheryl said. "He does say that he thinks about it.
"I can’t imagine the torture of going through that, not being able to open your eyes or move or talk.”
A radio has been placed by Liam’s bedside to distract him, playing classic rock and NHL games with his favourite team, the Montreal Canadiens.
“A lot of us talking to him is reminding him that he’s safe and he’s at the hospital ... and that he is OK,” Marisa said.
Military career
The military was always a passion for her son, Cheryl said.
“Liam tried a few other things first, but the military was always what he wanted to do.”
A sign for Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, on Oct. 18, 2026, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire caused deaths and injuries. (Jennifer Gauthier/Reuters)
He enlisted in March 2024 and completed a tour in Latvia. He was training in Wainwright to prepare for a second Latvia tour.
As a military mother, Cheryl said she knows the risks that soldiers face but never expected something like this.
“I never dreamt something would be two hours from home.”
Military, community support
Both women said the support from family, friends and the wider community has given them strength.
Their priority now is Liam and his recovery, not the fire or the military’s response. Three investigations are underway.
“That was a freak accident,” Marisa said. “They couldn’t have predicted that that would happen. And the military has been supportive of everything.
"We’ll have questions later but we are definitely focused on Liam.”

“Nothing [about] what started the fire will change where we’re at,” Cheryl said. “I have no interest in that at this moment. … They don’t stop war because it’s windy or anything like that. They have to prepare in all conditions.
“Do I place blame? Am I angry right now? No. I wish it wouldn’t have happened.”
Marisa and Cheryl say this Remembrance Day has new meaning for them.
“Hold your family a little closer,” said Marisa. “You never know what could happen. Honestly. Hold them close.”
“I didn’t hope that this would happen to my son,” said Cheryl. “I wish it hadn’t. But I’m proud for him.”

articles.title: Bomb threats force planes into emergency landings at several European airports
articles.summary: Bomb threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe on ‌Thursday morning, the latest in a series of threats targeting flights in Europe.

image.caption: An Aer Lingus Airbus A320 plane is seen at Evreux military air base after the flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to France following a bomb threat on Thursday. (Gonzalo Fuentes/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
Bomb threats forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe on ‌Thursday morning, the latest in a series of threats targeting flights in Europe.
No incendiary devices found after security checks carried out in several locations

Four airplanes heading to Prague received ‌bomb threats on Thursday ​and police were preparing ​for their landing, Czech police ​said on ⁠X, ⁠adding ‌they assessed the credibility of the threats ⁠as low.

"Nevertheless, we are not underestimating ‌the threat, which is why all necessary security ​measures have ⁠been activated with minimal ⁠impact on ⁠passengers ⁠and ​airport operations," police said. "After ​landing, ⁠all aircraft will undergo pyrotechnic inspections."
Bulgarian ⁠officials reported three aircraft making emergency landings because of bomb threats.
Airplanes flying from Copenhagen and Madrid landed in Sofia, the interior ‌minister said, according to broadcaster bTV.
A third aircraft, from London, landed in Plovdiv, local media said.
Polish airlines LOT said on Thursday that a ‌flight from Warsaw to Brussels landed safely at its ​destination after a ​security warning and no threat was confirmed.

"Following ​receipt of information ⁠regarding a ⁠potential security ‌threat to flight LO235 from Warsaw to Brussels, the flight ⁠crew was notified of the situation and conducted ‌an onboard inspection in accordance with established procedures. No suspicious items ​were found," a LOT ⁠spokesperson said.
Unclear who's responsible for threats
The aircraft landed ⁠at Brussels Airport, ⁠where ⁠security services ​carried out an additional inspection ​of ⁠the plane.
Aer Lingus flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome landed safely at Evreux ​airport, 100 km west of Paris, ​after being diverted as a security precaution, the Irish airline said in a statement.
A Finnair plane from Helsinki was safely escorted to its scheduled landing in Rome by the Italian air force, a source close to the matter said.
On Tuesday, at least seven flights and a cruise ship received bomb ​threats, causing disruption at airports across Europe, although no devices were discovered.

items: String of bomb threats on flights, cruise ship disrupt travel across Europe
Another cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps Europe, leaving food spoiled

blocks.text: While ⁠no country has attributed blame for the threats, they come at ⁠a time when European officials have been blaming ⁠both Russia ⁠and Iran for what ​they describe as "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage. Moscow and Tehran ​both deny any ⁠such campaign.

Drone incursions have periodically forced flight delays and cancellations in Europe and, this week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several countries across the continent. Some experts said hoax bomb threats could be part of a similar pattern of low-cost, deniable disruption ⁠efforts.

articles.title: Poland arrests 4 accused of spying for Russia
articles.summary: Poland has charged four people with espionage, saying they were sending information to Moscow. Two more have been accused of shipping military components to Russia.

image.caption: Poland's Internal Security Agency, known as ABW, investigates espionage, terrorism and threats to national securityImage: Krzysztof Zatycki/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Polish authorities said Thursday that they had arrested six people over alleged military component shipments to Russia, four of whom have been charged with espionage.
Investigators said the group illegally supplied Moscow with significant quantities of parts used to manufacture ammunition and weapons systems despite an embargo.
What are the suspects accused of?

Four suspects, including the Russian woman, were charged with espionage and placed in pretrial detention for three months, Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) said. The other two are subject to non-custodial restrictions.
All six also face allegations of violating rules governing international trade in goods and technologies of strategic importance to national defense and international security.
"Russia is subject to a strict embargo in this area, and this operation was designed to circumvent it," Siemoniak told reporters.
The suspects are five Poles aged 25 to 52 and a 37-year-old Russian woman, intelligence coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak said.
Germany holds Ukrainian on suspicion of spying for Russia
Why is Poland concerned about Russian operations?
Poland, an EU and NATO member, is a major supporter of Ukraine and the main transit route for Western military and humanitarian aid to the country.
Siemoniak said nearly 100 people had been charged in ABW espionage and sabotage investigations since January 1, 2024.

Warsaw has repeatedly accused Russia of sabotage since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. On Tuesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland had foiled a possible provocation at its border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave.
The Russian Embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Kremlin has consistently denied conducting sabotage operations in NATO countries.

articles.title: NUP House members willing to disclose their amendments in proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: House NUP members are willing to disclose the budget amendments they included in the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027, Deputy =Speaker Ronaldo Puno of Antipolo said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 6:38pm

Members of the National Unity Party (NUP) in the House of Representatives are willing to disclose the budget amendments they included in the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027, Deputy Speaker Ronaldo Puno of Antipolo said Thursday.

Puno made the announcement after the NUP’s dialogue with the People’s Budget Coalition, which earlier flagged House amendments for the 2027 budget for supposed lack of documentation and stamp of approval by the concerned government agency.
“We fully support disclosure [of budget amendments]. In fact, today, I made a disclosure and explanation to the People's Budget Coalition on projects on my district,” Puno said in a press conference.
“I have informed them that any congressman in the National Unity Party is willing to provide them with such details. And we think anybody in Congress has the obligation to do this,” Puno added.
Puno said NUP is willing to show the trail from where the project proposal originated until it was included in the House-approved version.

“In fact, we went a little bit beyond that, that it must follow the bottom-up budget approach. Meaning to say, it has to begin with the barangay, go to the local government, eventually go to the Regional Development Council, then it goes to the agency. There's no reason why these things will not be documented,” Puno said.

Likewise, Puno said that the NUP will push for the inclusion of a special provision which will allow the Department of Agriculture (DA) to location of eight farm to market roads that it proposed to Congress with wrong coordinates.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian earlier said that the Senate will remove P8 billion worth of projects included in the proposed budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways due to lack of documentation.
Sought for comment on this action, Puno supported Gatchalian’s position.
“We believe that if it has no documentation, it has no right to be there [in the budget],” Puno said.
“We know the Senate is planning to eliminate them, [and] we will not object,” Puno added.

House appropriations panel senior vice chairperson Abet Garcia of Bataan, for his part, said that amendments introduced by lawmakers in the national budget are made based on requests from many sectors which are not easy to balance.

“The requests [for Congress to increase their budget on certain projects and items], they do not only come from government agencies. There are also requests from local government units. These requests are the ones that us members of the House try to address to balance the need to fund the needs of the people in a local and national level scale,” Garcia said.

“So, with limited resources, it's really a balancing act. And during the budget hearings, we learn about the absorptive capacity of implementing agencies, and which projects should be prioritized, to come up with a final version of the House General Appropriations Bill. And if I may say, in the end, wala pong masaya kasi limited yung budget, but we have to come up with a workable budget,” Garcia added.
(Nobody really ends up happy because of limited resources.) — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Who are the Cabinet members of BARMM chief Macacua’s admin?
articles.summary: The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region's ministries and offices

blocks.text: CABINET. BARMM Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua announces on November 5, 2026 the newly constituted Cabinet of his administration, marking what he hailed as a "defining moment" in Bangsamoro history.
BARMM FB live/Screenshot
The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region's ministries and offices

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Following the historic inauguration of the region’s first-ever elected parliament, Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua officially announced on Thursday, November 5 the newly constituted Cabinet of his administration, marking what he hailed as a “defining moment” in Bangsamoro history.

The announcement comes on the heels of a vetting and screening process conducted by a special committee, designed to select leaders based on “competence, professional experience, integrity, and a strict commitment to moral governance.”
“To my fellow Bangsamoro, this government is yours,” Macacua declared. “We will pursue a policy of moral governance, integrity, and accountability.”

blocks.caption: Macacua is BARMM Parliament’s first elected chief minister | The wRap

blocks.text: The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region’s ministries and offices:

items: Senior Minister: Member of Parliament (MP) Abunawas Maslamama
Cabinet Secretary: Abdullah M. Cusain
Bangsamoro Attorney-General’s Office: Judge Duque D. Kadatuan
Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education: MP Atty. Naguib G. Sinarimbo
Ministry of Social Services and Development: Atty. Alirakim Munder
Ministry of Health: MP Atty. Jimael Salam D. Salliman
Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform: MP Atty. Ishak V. Mastura
Ministry of Interior and Local Government: Jordan S. Bayam
Ministry of Public Order and Safety: Datu Jomar U. Midtimbang
Ministry of Labor and Employment: MP Atty. Kitem D. Kadatuan, Jr.
Ministry of Trade and Investment, and Tourism: Atty. Faizal M. Padate
Ministry of Indigenous People’s Affair: MP Jo Genna Jover
Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management: Atty. Ubaida C. Pacasem
Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources, and Energy: MP Akmad Brahim
Ministry of Science and Technology: MP Hanie Bud
Ministry of Human Settlement and Development: MP Engr. Rashdi T. Adiong
Ministry of Transportation and Communication: Termizie G. Masahud
Ministry of Public Works: Engr. Basir M. Ibrahim

blocks.text: Macacua acknowledged that the governance workload ahead is immense, but emphasized that the regional leadership’s resolve remains even greater. He underscored the administration’s dedication to preserving the hard-won gains of the peace process.

“We commit to sustaining the gains of the peace process and ensuring that the dividends of autonomy are felt in every household and every community,” Macacua said. “Together, with the continued support of our national government, local government units, and our partners, we will write a new chapter of peace, prosperity, and dignity for our people.”

Reflecting on the big tasks ahead, Macacua underscored that the newly formed administration will vigorously pursue moral governance—the foundational policy initiated by former chief minister Al Haj Murad Ebrahim.

“My fellow Bangsamoro, this government is yours,” Macacua stated. “We will pursue and vanish your moral or moral governance that had been initiated by former chief minister Al Haj Murad Ebrahim. Indeed, the work ahead is immense, but our resolve is greater.”
Macacua also committed his administration to sustaining the ongoing peace process and ensuring that the tangible dividends of regional autonomy reach every household and community.

He also expressed gratitude for the continued, collaborative backing of the national government, inter-governmental units, and international and local partners in cultivating peace, prosperity, and dignity for the Bangsamoro land and its people. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Finland court jails captain and crew member over Baltic cable sabotage
articles.summary: Finland seized the Fitburg freighter last year over the suspected sabotage of cables linking Helsinki and Tallinn. It's one of several incidents of damaged infrastructure in the Baltic since Russia's…

image.caption: The Fitburg was en route to Israel when it was seized by Finnish authorities in the Baltic Sea for alleged sabotageImage: Finnish Police/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Finnish court on Thursday convicted the Russian captain and a senior crew member of the cargo ship Fitburg for damaging two undersea telecommunications cables in the Gulf of Finland last year.
The Helsinki District Court found the two defendants guilty of "aggravated criminal damage."
It said in a statement that they had intentionally dragged the ship's anchor along the seabed for around 130 kilometers (81 miles).
The captain was sentenced to three and a half years in jail, while the crew member, an Azerbaijani citizen, was sentenced to two years and 10 months.
They were also ordered to jointly pay around €1.9 million ($2.1 million) in damages, the Reuters news agency reported, with the captain to pay about €85,000 more.
The defendants denied any wrongdoing and have challenged Finland's jurisdiction in the case.
What else do we know about the Fitburg freighter?
Finnish authorities seized the vessel on December 31 on suspicion that it had damaged cables linking Finland's capital, Helsinki, and Tallinn, Estonia.
Finnish police at the time said the ship had been dragging its anchor for hours when it was discovered.
The Fitburg and its 14-member crew had been en route to the port of Haifa, Israel, from the Russian city of St. Petersburg when the incident occurred.

Finland has stepped up efforts to protect its undersea infrastructure following a series of incidents involving cables and pipelines in the Baltic Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

articles.title: 'Big chance' of Bato dela Rosa getting arrested, says NBI's Matibag
articles.summary: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday expressed belief that there is a big possibility that embattled Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa will be located and arrested…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 6:27pm

National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday expressed belief that there is a big possibility that embattled Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa will be located and arrested soon.
In an ambush interview, Matibag said authorities may start conducting operations, based on intelligence reports, to determine Dela Rosa's exact whereabouts.
"Baka any time soon we'll have some operations just to eliminate 'yung areas that we've identified based on the intel reports that we're having," the NBI chief said.
(Maybe any time soon we'll have some operations just to eliminate the areas that we've identified based on the intel reports that we're having.)
"I think with the information that we're getting, baka malaki 'yung tsansa (there might be a big chance)," he added.
Asked if Dela Rosa is hiding in Mindanao, Matibag said he could not tell for sure.
"Basta we have strong belief na nandito siya sa Pilipinas. But though, that's a possibility," he said.
(We just have a strong belief that he is here in the Philippines. But though, that's a possibility.)

Dela Rosa has been issued an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court (ICC) in relation to the drug war of former president Rodrigo Duterte. The senator was chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP) at the time the war on drugs was implemented.

The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) has raised a P50-million reward for the arrest of Dela Rosa, who according to Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic" Remulla is considered "armed and dangerous."
Remulla also said authorities were also negotiating with a group protecting the senator to secure his surrender and prevent a potentially violent confrontation.
Duterte, meanwhile, is detained at the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands, while awaiting his crimes against humanity trial this month. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation
articles.summary: Five of France's unions have joined a wave of strikes and protests in a national day of action.

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action.
The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow-vest" movement and workers.
Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence".
The five unions have combined forces across the public and private sector, with demands for higher wages to combat the cost of living and protected public services.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said that 70,000 police and gendarmes are being deployed, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.
More than 250 separate actions are planned for 5 November, with some disruption reported in schools, hospitals and public transport.
Workers have also been asked to halt production at oil refineries, and France is expected to import more electricity than it produces on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.

A coalition of unions has urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.
The head of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase: "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month."

The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028.

Some 81 lycées - high schools that cater for 15-18 year-olds - were shut on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry. It added that about 17.5% of primary schools too were affected by the strikes.
Large numbers are expected on the streets, especially in the capital, and Léon said she would be happy if 800,000 people turned out.
One union leader Sophie Binet, who called it the "great day of convergence", added: "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level; the strike must take over."

Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too.

articles.title: Who’s next for Maharlika Fund after Joel Consing?
articles.summary: 'Whatever we have achieved can only grow from here,' says Maharlika Investment Corporation's top boss, Joel Consing, who's set to step down on November 23

blocks.text: PCEO. Maharlika Investment Corporation President and CEO Joel Consing speaks to the media on Thursday, November 5.
Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler
'Whatever we have achieved can only grow from here,' says Maharlika Investment Corporation's top boss, Joel Consing, who's set to step down on November 23

items: Rafael 'Joel' Consing Jr. will conclude his term as head of the Maharlika Investment Corporation on November 23, with no confirmed successor announced.
Consing plans to leave behind extensive research and documentation for his successor, emphasizing the importance of institutional culture and continuity within the organization.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Rafael “Joel” Consing Jr. knows exactly when his time at the Maharlika Investment Corporation (MIC) ends.
November 23. Five o’clock sharp.
But who will take over the country’s still-young sovereign wealth fund? That part we don’t yet know.
“It’s been reported my term as PCO ends at the end of this month. Any announcement on the transition will come from the Palace,” Consing told reporters on Thursday, November 5.

blocks.caption: Who’s next for Maharlika Fund after Joel Consing?

blocks.text: Leaving too is MIC’s chief investment and operating officer Kheed Nielsen Ng, who is co-terminus with Consing.

Though MIC’s boss has kept mum on who might take his place, one name making the rounds is Finance Undersecretary Ma. Angela “Angel” Ignacio, who oversees the Department of Finance’s (DOF) Government Corporations and Investments Group.

Ignacio joined the DOF in February 2026, but she is no stranger to Finance Secretary Frederick Go or Consing himself. All three previously worked at the now-defunct Office of the Special Assistant to the President for Investment and Economic Affairs, which Go headed before taking over the DOF. Ignacio served as an undersecretary, while Consing was its executive director before taking the helm at Maharlika.
When asked about it, Consing offered no confirmation. The appointment, he said, remains the call of the President.
So after three years at the helm, does Consing have any parting instructions?
“I don’t give instructions to my successors,” Consing said. “No instructions, just a suggested path forward.”

What he is leaving behind, however, is paperwork. Lots of it. MIC departments are assembling year-end reports. For his part, Consing is preparing a compendium of his research papers, which he intends to share with his successor and the Land Bank of the Philippines.
“All the stuff that we’re doing actually came as a result of my research background. And I’ve written much more than what we’ve done. I’m turning over all of those to my successor,” he said.

There is also the matter of preserving the institutional culture, arguably just as important a matter, especially for a fledgling sovereign wealth fund that found its inception marred by governance concerns.

“One of the messages that I’ve always told them, and I continue to tell them, and which I will tell them on the 23rd when I leave is: They are the legacy of MIC, apart from what it aims to achieve. And they’re also my continuation, my transition. So hence, whatever we have achieved can only grow from here,” he said.
As for his own next act, Consing said he is leaving government, though he did not rule out returning someday.
Before joining the government in 2023, he was the chief financial officer of Enrique Razon Jr.’s International Container Terminal Services Inc. and managing director at HSBC.
For now, he says he is occupied with making sure MIC is left “very, very strong” and with handing over a “very healthy organization” to his successor. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
articles.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and…

image.caption: This Airbus A320, which was diverted to Evreux airbase, was the first of multiple disruptions to become public knowledgeImage: Gonzalo Fuentes/REUTERS

blocks.text: At least a dozen commercial flights made either unscheduled or high-alert landings in Austria, France, Italy, Belgium, Czechia, Spain, Serbia and Bulgaria, according to authorities in the various countries.

Planes made unscheduled landings in Evreux, France; in Vienna, Austria; and in Bulgaria. A flight from Finland landed in Rome as scheduled but with a military escort, and various others touched down at their scheduled destinations across the continent but amid security alerts.
The incident in France became public knowledge first, but the other similar reports soon followed.
No initial signs of a genuine threat, EU says still 'too early' to say if cases linked
This comes after a series of bomb threats leveled against several European flights earlier this week, prompting similar unscheduled landings.
Tuesday's incidents turned out to be hoaxes, and preliminary information shows no sign of dangerous materials reported in Thursday's threats as yet.
The European Union Commissioner for Transport and Tourism, Apostolos Tzitzikostas, wrote online that any threats against civilians were unacceptable.
"It is too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked," Tzitzikostas said. "National investigations remain ongoing."
What happened in the subsequent alerts across Europe?
News of a series of diversions and bomb scares trickled out during the course of the day, particularly late in the morning:

items: Finland's Finnair carrier reported that two planes landed at their scheduled destinations but amid security scares.
One Finnair flight from Helsinki to Rome landed with a military escort. Another plane from the Finnish capital, operated by Jettime, also landed in Vienna as scheduled.
A Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw made an unscheduled landing in Vienna.
Bulgaria reported three aircraft making emergency landings because of bomb threats.
Three Ryanair flights to Sofia — from Copenhagen, Madrid and London Stansted — also all landed under high alert.
Two of them touched down in Sofia as scheduled and one diverted to Plovdiv, the airport's CEO said.

blocks.caption: The Bulgarian threats concerned Ryanair flights bound for Sofia, two of which landed in Sofia and one in PlovdivImage: Stoyan Nenov/REUTERS

items: Italian news outlets and the Reuters news agency reported, citing airport sources, that two planes — an Aegean Airlines flight from Thessaloniki and a Ryanair flight from Porto — landed at the Malpensa airport in Milan as scheduled after receiving bomb alerts on Thursday morning.
Police in Madrid said that three flights at the Spanish capital's airport were affected by what they called hoax threats, saying that security forces searched the area and ruled out any risk.
Police in the Czech Republic later said that they were preparing officials at Prague airport for four landings after threats of improvised explosive devices being on board.

"We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech police said. "Nevertheless, we do not underestimate the threat, which is why all necessary security measures have been activated with the least possible impact on passengers and airport operations."
On Thursday afternoon, Air Serbia issued a statement saying a flight from Belgrade to Bucharest landed safely at its destination after receiving a bomb threat.

blocks.text: What do we know about the first incident outside Paris?
An Airbus A320 plane has been diverted to the Evreux airbase to the west of Paris following a bomb threat.
The office of French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced the incident on Thursday, saying it was monitoring the situation "in real time."
The flight was headed from Dublin, Ireland, to the Italian capital of Rome.
Tracking websites showed the plane, part of the Aer Lingus fleet, sharply deviating its course as it was around Paris' airspace and heading towards the more isolated airfield in Evreux.
France's air force said that it dispatched planes "as soon as the incident was reported."
"The aircraft has been diverted and is being escorted to Evreux airfield," it said.
Lecornu's office subsequently confirmed that the plane, part of the Aer Lingus fleet, had landed safely at the airfield.

blocks.caption: The Evreux airbase in northeastern France, not far from Paris, is typically used for military purposes not commercial flights [FILE: July 9, 2025]Image: JP Pariente/SIPA/picture alliance

blocks.text: What happened during the earlier disruptions?
The prior threats to commercial flights this week turned out to be hoaxes that nevertheless caused diversions and major security mobilizations.
In one case, the Italian air force escorted a plane to its emergency landing.
The threats targeted airlines including Poland's LOT, Scandinavian Airlines, Wizz Air and Ryanair.

While it's not yet clear if there is a link, these disruptions to commercial aviation also coincided with a series of apparent cyberattacks targeting freezer units in major supermarkets and even French blood banks.
All the cases remain nascent, but have the potential hallmarks of so-called hybrid attacks designed to cause maximum disruption with minimal effort and resources.

articles.title: 2 tagged in Bacoor pet crematorium case surrender to NBI; charges to be filed
articles.summary: The husband and wife allegedly responsible for the dumped pet remains in Bulacan have surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), according to Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday.

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 6:09pm
The husband and wife allegedly responsible for the dumped pet remains in Bulacan have surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), according to Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday.
Matibag thanked the NBI Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) for cracking the case, calling it a “major breakthrough”.

“Nakuha kaagad natin yung person responsible dun sa pagbabaon nung mga pets na supposed to be na-cremate. Dalawa yung individual natin na subject ngayon, which is under our custody, voluntarily na pumunta dito sa atin at nakuhanan natin yung story kung paano ito nangyari and we will be filing the necessary charges dito sa mga individuals na ito,” Matibag said in a press conference.

(We got the person responsible for burying these pets that were supposed to be cremated. Two of the individuals that are under our custody voluntarily went here and we got the story on how this happened and we will be filing the necessary charges against these individuals.)
According to Matibag, the couple who owns the Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite also owned a crematorium in San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan.
The pets in Bacoor were being sent to San Jose Del Monte for cremation, and then the ashes were supposed to be returned.

“Ang findings na natin dito, Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium, wala siyang facility, wala siyang equipment to do the cremation. So pinadala niya doon. Malaki yung volume ng dumarating,” Matibag said.

(Our findings here: Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium, they do not have the facility; they do not have the equipment to do the cremation. So they were brought there. There was a large volume being brought there.)
“So ang ginawa nila, linibing nila,” he added, citing the couple’s testimony. (So what they did, they buried them.)

Matibag said that the lack of proper cremation facilities points to evidence of estafa, as well as violations of the Consumer Protection Act. The NBI is also determining if there were violations in health and sanitation standards over the transferring of the dead pets from Bacoor to San Jose Del Monte.
The NBI has pinpointed three dumpsites, Matibag said.
When no more ashes were being returned to the Bacoor crematorium, the crematorium itself came up with ashes. Matibag said that no cremation took place at all.

Matibag said that the NBI will file six cases initially, since there were six complainants who came forward to the agency. However, Matibag said that there was already enough evidence for them to also file a case before the prosecutor’s office.
A large portion of the case has already been solved, Matibag said. He urged any other possible complainants to come forward, since there was already plenty of evidence.

However, Matibag said that they were also determining the liability of other parties, especially since the Bacoor pet crematorium was able to operate for so long even if they did not have the proper facilities.
The NBI is also attempting to get an Immigration Lookout Bulletin Order for other people who may be involved in the case, so that they will not escape, according to Matibag. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: [Rappler Investigates] Who’s taking care of our dead?
articles.summary: How could the living get through their own painful experience of saying their final goodbyes if embalmers weren’t there to help preserve the memory of their loved ones?

blocks.text: Many of us finished paying homage to our beloved departed in the past weekend or so, offering prayers and remembering them in very special ways.

There might have been different circumstances of their passing and varying means of sending them to their final resting place. But one common thing they must have all undergone was dignified preparation of their remains for grieving family members left behind to bid them tearful, sometimes painful, farewells.
This is made possible only by the careful handling of their bodies by embalmers, who are often faceless individuals because they remain behind the scenes in mortuaries.

Researcher Eirene Manatlao partnered with Henry Luce Foundation scholar Jake Gomez to take a peek into the little known world of embalmers — often stereotyped as uneducated or unclean because they handle the dead.

Jake discovered that embalmers need a “high school diploma, at least 140 hours of instruction from an accredited institution, and proof that they have embalmed at least 10 cadavers within a year.” After about two months of classroom instruction, they spend another month working on real cadavers in funeral homes.
They are required to pass an exam to obtain a license that must be renewed every three years.

In 2018, there were an estimated 5,000 licensed embalmers on record in the country but the number may not be as accurate. Today, very rough estimates put the count at a little over 6,000. Depending on employers, they get benefits and privileges on top of minimum wage. Others get paid by the number of bodies they handle, charging about P1,000 per body.
Eirene spoke to two embalmers and found a common vulnerability — processing the remains of babies that made them cry because they, too, are parents.

They’ve had to contend with the stigma associated with the profession and with common misperceptions. Their work requires attention to detail, taking as long as four hours per cadaver, sometimes longer, depending on the body’s physical condition.
One of them, Joycel Regalado, pointed out the importance of what they do: “Kung wala kami, sino ang mag-aayos ng patay?” (If we weren’t here, who would take care of the dead?)
Very true, for how could the living get through their own painful experience of saying their final goodbyes if embalmers weren’t there to help preserve the memory of their loved ones?

Meanwhile, we, who are still here, are reminded to continue with the business and concerns of living: how to better cope with the looming Super El Niño and its effects on farmers, as well as the persisting energy crisis that has caused electricity bills to soar. We will be doing more stories on this extreme weather event that is threatening to break records and last through early next year.

The Visayas is expected to be problematic even if more than half of the Visayas grid’s power generation mix comes from renewable energy sources. Reporter John Sitchon, who is based in Cebu, warns that multiple red alerts are expected in the region in 2027 due to rising demand and unstable energy supply. He mapped the Visayas energy mix across the region’s five island sub-grids in Cebu, Bohol, Panay, Negros, and Leyet-Samar. Take a look here.

Researcher Shay Du looked into the affordability of going solar for household rooftops as a way of coping with mounting electricity bills. Estimated costs of putting up such solar panels range from P80,000 to P200,000 for average households, up to over half a million pesos for larger houses.

There are financing options available, according to Shay. Government employees considering going solar can take out loans from the Government Service Insurance System, while private employees can expect loans from the Social Security System by 2027. Home improvement loans via Pag-IBIG are also available.

Let’s not lose sight of other big issues that might get past us because of more urgent daily living concerns. Let’s continue monitoring how public funds are being allocated and who will be chosen by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as new members of the Supreme Court, including his pick as replacement of Chief Justice Gesmundo, who retires this Friday, November 6.
Till Thursday after next!

articles.title: PSA finds evidence of Joseph Sy's 'fake' records
articles.summary: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said Thursday it found evidence showing that embattled businessman Joseph Sy procured fake documents during his birth registration process.

blocks.text: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said Thursday it found evidence showing that embattled businessman Joseph Sy procured fake documents during his birth registration process.

PSA Legal Service Director Atty. Eliezer Ambatali said this during the continuation of the Senate Committee on Justice and Human Rights’ hearing into the case of Sy---a nickel businessman who was previously arrested after his biometrics matched those of a Chinese citizen Chen Zhong Zhen.
Ambatali said the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) has already filed a petition for the cancellation of the birth records of Sy.

“Doon sa investigation namin…investigation ng Fraud Management Division ito ng PSA, we found out that there is evidence that would say na merong…mga procurement ng fake documents during the registration,” Ambatali said.
(In our investigation, conducted by the PSA’s Fraud Management Division, we discovered evidence indicating that fake documents were procured during Sy’s registration process.)

“This type of fraud is the second type. It happens at the source, during the registration. So these are fake ‘yung baptismal certificate…hindi makita ‘yung birth records ng mga magulang, hindi rin namin makita ‘yung mga records ng hilot or ‘yung attending person during the time of birth,” he added.

(This type of fraud is the second type. It happens at the source, during the registration. For instance, we found that his baptismal certificates are fake; we cannot locate his parents’ birth records nor any records from his birth attendant or the person who assisted during his birth.)
Suspected of being a Chinese national parading as a Filipino, Sy was arrested by Philippine authorities in 2025 when he arrived at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport from Hong Kong.
But the Supreme Court (SC) First Division ordered last month the release of Sy, ruling in favor of his petition for habeas corpus.
The Bureau of Immigration (BI) said it respected the SC’s resolution on the petition, but clarified that the Court did not settle the matter of Sy’s nationality.
Fingerprints
Meanwhile, Bureau of Immigration (BI) Deputy Commissioner Atty. Joel Alejandro Nacnac also confirmed during the hearing that the fingerprints of Sy matched those of Chinese national Chen Zhong Zhen.
Committee chairperson Sen. Risa Hontiveros then asked when the fingerprints of Sy entered the BI database.
“Under our records, he is an applicant po ng returning resident visa way back in 1989. Subsequently, the permanent resident visa was approved in February of 1989,” Nacnac said.

“Later on, he also applied under RA 7919, it po ‘yung Alien Social Integration Program, which appears to be on record, March of 1996 na po. With this, ‘yung biometric records niya ay nakita at na-capture po ng Bureau,” he added.
(Later on, he also applied for the Alien Social Integration Program, which appears to be on record, March of 1996. With this, his biometric records were seen and captured by the Bureau.)
No show
Sy, who is the subject of the investigation, also failed to attend the hearing.
His lawyer, Alma Mallonga, said that the businessman called earlier this morning to say that he was in an emergency room of Makati Medical Center and “had been feeling unwell since last night.”

“Maybe part of it is the stress. The fact that he had been incarcerated for more than 491 days, Your Honor, and it’s just been less than three weeks since he was released,” Mallonga said, adding that her client also underwent certain “surgical procedures.”
Regardless, the lawyer said Sy had earlier expressed intent to attend the hearing.

Hontiveros, on the other hand, asked Sy’s lawyer to submit a medical certificate and instructed the committee secretary to coordinate with the Senate clinic to validate the condition of the embattled businessman.
The senator also said she is expecting that Sy will be attending the next committee hearing.
“Mr. Joseph Sy, inaasahan kita sa susunod na hearing. Kung kaya mo mag party-party, Baka kaya mo ring dumalo at harapin ang Senado ng Pilipinas,” Hontiveros said.
(Mr. Joseph Sy, I expect to see you at the next hearing. If you’re capable of partying, perhaps you’re also capable of attending and facing the Philippine Senate.) —LDF, GMA News
